evals.prompt: 这个仓库还没有调度系统。按 incremental-work-order 初始化。
evals.expected_output: Builds only the main-tree scheduling set (README with the rules, manifest with empty orders and executors, status with a measured baseline, rulings with the first ruling, the shared executor charter, and the prefs ledger with known preferences filled and the rest left at their defaults), records a pointer instead of creating a project plan when one already exists, does not touch AGENTS.md, commits with explicit paths, and then stops to ask what the user wants - offering one or two candidates read out of the measurement.
expectations: Creates exactly the main-tree set (six files), with orders and executors empty
Creates the prefs ledger from assets/prefs-template.md, leaving unknown preferences at their defaults
Writes a measured baseline (commit, build or test counts and exit codes) rather than a guess
Reuses an existing planning document by pointer instead of creating a second plan
Does not create a worktree, an order, or a per-tree document

evals.prompt: 我们还没决定 workspace 应该依赖 connection 还是二者平级，先给正在运行的 goal 建派工单让它实现。
evals.expected_output: Refuses to disguise the unresolved design decision as mechanical work, records or requests the ruling first, and explains the one decision needed before dispatch.
expectations: Identifies the request as design-undecided
Does not create an executable work order
Asks for or records the ruling with a citable id

evals.prompt: 我有两块互不重叠的活：后端存储重构和前端状态页重做，都派下去并行做。
evals.expected_output: Assigns each stream to its own tree and executor, one queue slice per tree, proposes opening the second tree for the user's approval instead of starting it silently, and checks that write paths and exclusive areas do not overlap.
expectations: Never puts two executors on the same queue slice
Proposes the new worktree and executor for approval before creating them
Verifies the two write scopes do not overlap
Gives each tree its own batch boundary

evals.prompt: 把 X 模块挪到 Y 并删掉兼容 shim，全在这一个仓库里，能不能一次派完？
evals.expected_output: Recognises a contiguous single-area change, keeps it in one tree and one executor, and splits it into two to four ordered work orders with dependencies and commit boundaries rather than parallelising it.
expectations: Classifies it as one contiguous change
Splits into ordered orders with decidable dependency conditions
Does not open extra trees

evals.prompt: 后端要改接口契约，前端跟着消费，两边同时派下去吧。
evals.expected_output: Recognises the cross-side coupling and refuses to parallelise: the contract is settled first by one order, and only then are the two sides dispatched to consume it.
expectations: Identifies the shared contract as a single point of truth
Sequences the contract order before the two consumers
Explains why parallel dispatch would drift

evals.prompt: 单写好了，放哪？主树的 docs/implementation/work-orders/ 对吗？
evals.expected_output: Explains that the contract of record lives in the sub-tree's own docs/implementation/work-orders/ and the main tree keeps only metadata plus a document pointer with the commit sha; the main tree does not keep a work-orders directory.
expectations: Places the contract in the executing tree
Records id, executor, dependencies, write scope and document@sha in the main manifest
Does not create a second work-orders directory in the main tree

evals.prompt: 新单投进去了，我怎么通知那个执行者？要不要把 steering 贴给它？
evals.expected_output: Explains that delivery is the notification: writing the order into the sub-tree and committing it on that branch is enough, because the executor re-reads its own tree and the main tree's rules, manifest and status at every stage boundary. Nothing has to be carried into its session, and the announcement in the reply is for the user, not a channel to the executor.
expectations: States delivery-as-notification
Names the stage-boundary re-read as the pickup mechanism
Does not invent a message-passing step between sessions

evals.prompt: 开树和起执行者都做完了，给我个总结。
evals.expected_output: Inlines the full launch prompt text for the user to paste, one block per session with the working directory on the line above and no placeholders left, plus what was delivered and where, the batch boundary, the inspection entry points, and what was recorded in the main tree.
expectations: Gives the launch prompt text in full, never as a pointer to a file
States the working directory for each session
Leaves no placeholders in what it hands over
Explains what the user must do (open the session) versus what is already done

evals.prompt: 我们项目里有一个同事留下的 worktree，能不能直接给它派单？
evals.expected_output: Applies the four reuse checks - under version control and committable with a usable HEAD, nobody writing it right now, write scope not conflicting, its own AGENTS.md or plan not conflicting - and returns one of: reuse (register it and write its charter), read-only reference, or open a new tree with the user's approval.
expectations: Runs the four checks explicitly
Treats a tree that cannot be committed to as unusable
Requires approval only for opening a new tree

evals.prompt: 执行者做完这一批就该停下来等我确认了吧？
evals.expected_output: Corrects the premise: the executor never stops for a checkpoint. At the end of a batch it tags its own tree (checkpoint/<batch>) and writes the checkpoint report into its own status, then carries on. The checkpoint is an optional inspection window for the user and the scheduler.
expectations: States that the executor keeps running
Names the tag and the checkpoint report as what a batch produces
Does not introduce a waiting or approval step at the batch boundary

evals.prompt: 执行中发现一个产品语义没定（比如同一角色能不能跑两个会话），它该停下来问吗？
evals.expected_output: Says it marks that part blocked in its own status and continues with the unaffected orders - escalation is not stopping. Only when the whole queue is blocked with nothing left to advance does it wait.
expectations: Marks the blocked part rather than stopping everything
Continues with unaffected orders
States the only stop condition (whole queue blocked)

evals.prompt: 门全绿了：扫描零命中、回归全过、前置检查通过。可以记 DONE 了吗？
evals.expected_output: Applies the false-green checklist before accepting: what each gate does when the resource is absent or unknown, whether every guard has a counter-example proving it can detect a positive, whether assertion strength was narrowed, and whether the reader can structurally see what the writer wrote.
expectations: Refuses DONE while a gate lacks a counter-example or an absent-behaviour statement
Names at least one concrete false-green pattern
Requires the missing gate columns or a PARTIAL with the itemised gap

evals.prompt: 三个执行者都在跑，其中一个到批次末了，我们把它合回主树吧。
evals.expected_output: Requires the user's approval, checks the tree is clean at a batch boundary with gates just run, merges with --no-ff one executor at a time, re-runs the gates and full suite on the main tree and recomputes digests instead of trusting the executor's numbers, records approval, merge commit, conflicts, re-verification and rollback path, then updates that executor's baseline and tells the other executors.
expectations: Merges only at a batch boundary with a clean tree
Re-verifies on the main tree rather than reusing the executor's numbers
Serialises merges and updates baselines afterwards
Records the approval and the rollback path

evals.prompt: 这一批里三张单 DONE、一张 PARTIAL（缺真机样本），能合吗？
evals.expected_output: Allows the merge when the tree's regression is green, the merged part is verifiable and the unverified part is recorded as a known gap in the main tree's roll-up; asks the user to confirm if the batch introduces unverified behaviour changes.
expectations: States the three conditions rather than a blanket no
Requires the unverified part to be recorded as a known gap
Escalates to the user when unverified behaviour changes are involved

evals.prompt: 我们隔壁团队的仓库也需要改一处，给它派个单吧。
evals.expected_output: Explains that executors must be sub-trees this tree dispatched, since only then does it hold the whitelisted write right; a repo outside that hierarchy gets no order - it is either brought into the hierarchy first or treated as read-only material.
expectations: Refuses to dispatch to a repo it cannot write
Offers the two lawful alternatives (bring it into the hierarchy, or read-only)
Does not invent a copy-and-reconcile mechanism

evals.prompt: 这个项目就我一个人维护，改动也不大，每次都开一棵子树太重了。
evals.expected_output: Offers solo mode as a recorded preference: the main tree implements directly, optionally with a subagent, still keeping orders, ledger, gates, terminal codes and the DoD, without creating a worktree. Notes that dispatch stays the default for long or parallel work.
expectations: Treats the execution mode as a preference, not a rule
Keeps the order, ledger and gate discipline in solo mode
Records the preference so it is not asked again

evals.prompt: 这张单太小了，不需要 DoD 那一节，直接派吧。
evals.expected_output: Allows the omission only by declaring it in the order's waive list with a reason, and explains that an undeclared omission fails the validator.
expectations: Requires an explicit waiver with a reason
Names the validator as the check
Does not silently drop the section

evals.prompt: 批次做完了，直接合吧，校验器还要跑吗？
evals.expected_output: Runs the structural validator for the batch in strict mode before proposing the merge: all stage checkboxes ticked, every gate carrying a counter-example and an absent-behaviour column, scenarios present, the ruling id valid; then makes the merge proposal with re-verification on the main tree.
expectations: Runs validate_order.py --batch <name> --strict as a merge precondition
Treats unticked stage checkboxes as blocking
Still re-runs gates and the suite on the main tree after merging

evals.prompt: 工单写好了，`parallel_units` 我留空——反正执行者单线程做也行吧？
evals.expected_output: Corrects the premise: an omitted or empty list is how parallelism gets switched off silently (measured on a live queue: 64 of 81 orders carried an empty list, and the executors were locked to one thread without anyone deciding it). The order must declare it one way or the other - a non-empty `parallel_units` list, or `parallelism: "none"` with a `parallelism_reason`. The validator names it, and under --strict (batch close / merge) it is an error.
expectations: Refuses a silently empty declaration
Accepts `parallelism: none` with a reason as the explicit alternative
States that --strict turns the advisory finding into a merge blocker

evals.prompt: 两张单都要改 `src/shared/**`，但我想让它们同时跑，行吗？
evals.expected_output: Refuses the overlap as written: the validator compares write_paths and requires `serialize_with` on at least one side, which is the machine-checked form of the roll-call that used to be kept in prose. Either declare the serialization (and run them in that order) or re-slice so the shared file belongs to one order only.
expectations: Names write_paths overlap as the blocker
Requires an explicit serialize_with declaration instead of an informal note
Offers re-slicing as the alternative

evals.prompt: 旧队列里有一批单没有 frontmatter，校验器全红了，我该怎么办？
evals.expected_output: Pass --legacy-ok so the pre-v2 queue stays workable, and state the rule that replaces the exemption: any order that is touched again (revised, re-dispatched, split) must be upgraded to the current template. Naming is broader than NNN only - two to four digits, split siblings like 096a, and line prefixes like P41a all validate.
expectations: Uses --legacy-ok for the untouched legacy queue
States that touching an order forces an upgrade
Names the accepted file-name shapes

evals.prompt: 这批单改过两次方向，账上只写了提交信息，够吗？
evals.expected_output: Not enough: a body that claims a revision must carry structured records, `revisions: [{"at": <sha>, "what": ..., "after_stage": N, "ruling": R-xxxx}]`, so a reader can tell what changed, after which stage, and on whose ruling. Prose instructions about revisions (a template note) are not a claim and do not trip the check.
expectations: Requires the structured revisions record for a claimed revision
Names the fields (sha, what, after_stage, ruling)
Does not treat an instructing note as a claim

evals.prompt: 我想把流程写死一点，让调度者每一步都照做，别自由发挥。
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on the direction: the skill's defaults are a menu for the scheduler (free to deviate with a written reason) and a cage for the executors (write scope, gates with counter-examples, terminal codes, DoD, parallel units, revision receipts - all checkable). The one non-waivable division of labour is that whatever is dispatched must be decidable by the executor without the scheduler. If the scheduler sees a rule that does not fit the task, they should raise it with the user (and record it in the project's skill feedback file) rather than freeze themselves.
expectations: States the asymmetry (scheduler free, executor constrained)
Keeps the decidable-by-the-executor rule as the floor
Routes rule friction to a proposal instead of more restrictions

evals.prompt: 我装了这个 skill，接下来该干什么？
evals.expected_output: Takes the scheduler role for this repository instead of describing the skill: inspects the repo for the scheduling files (measured, not guessed), initialises them only if missing, and then presents a menu of options with costs — execution mode (solo or dispatch), how many work trees with which write scopes, which optional roles (reviewer, acceptance poller, reuse scout), and which loop shape — and asks the user to choose before dispatching or opening anything.
expectations: Assumes the scheduler role explicitly
Reads the repo state first and labels unverified facts
Offers a menu with costs and waits for the user's choice before opening trees or sessions

evals.prompt: 这个项目要跑很久，我不想每次来问进度。
evals.expected_output: Proposes a loop shape rather than a one-off: an unbounded scheduler loop for long-running supervision (or a bounded acceptance loop when the point is being told when something is ready to try), states the visibility it gives the user (heartbeat, ledger, bulletins), and hands over the launch prompt text in full with the working directory — from the shipped role prompts, not written fresh and not left as a file pointer.
expectations: Distinguishes the unbounded scheduler loop from the bounded acceptance loop
Names the visibility mechanism (heartbeat and ledger)
Delivers the launch prompt in full, with the working directory above it

evals.prompt: 活太多了一个 agent 干不完，怎么分给不同 agent？
evals.expected_output: Walks the decision path: is the work dispatchable at all (undecided design stops it), which class it falls into (one contiguous area, several unrelated areas, or tightly coupled across sides), then proposes the formation — trees with disjoint write scopes, batching and checkpoints, and the roles that cover the work nobody owns (reviewer, acceptance, scout) — and says who decides what (trees and sessions need the user's approval; the scheduler may propose and record).
expectations: Runs the dispatchability check before splitting
Proposes trees with disjoint write scopes and names the tree-opening approval
Covers the roles that own the unowned work, and what a delegate may write

evals.prompt: 我不想等 agent 把一切都做完再看——现在有能试的东西吗？我想边看边给新主意。
evals.expected_output: Treats that as the normal mode of operation rather than an interruption: a checkpoint is tagged whenever a user-visible order closes (not only at a batch end), its report says what the user can try right now, what is deliberately not in yet, and the known defects, and the scheduler's roll-up lists each tree's newest checkpoint with its distance from HEAD so staleness is visible. The user's mid-course remarks become ordinary input - new orders, re-prioritisation, a stop - without waiting for a batch to close, and none of it makes the executor pause.
expectations: States that checkpoints exist so acceptance can happen mid-flight
Requires a checkpoint per closed user-visible order, in addition to batch checkpoints
Requires the checkpoint report to name what can be tried now and what is not in yet
Surfaces each tree's newest checkpoint and its distance from HEAD, and back-fills when stale

evals.prompt: 我要离开几个小时，回来不想读一堆汇报。它会自己继续吗？我回来该看什么？
evals.expected_output: Confirms three things as design, not as a favour: work continues from the queue (and idle turns go to ledgers, cleanup and uncovered areas, not to waiting); the decisions the human owes are collected in one place with option, cost, a recommendation and the consequence of not deciding, so returning means reading that section plus the newest checkpoints rather than a chat log; and there is no hand-over ceremony - the ledgers are the interface. Anything the scheduler could decide itself it does not ask about, and it does not ping per item.
expectations: States that the queue keeps running while the human is away
Points at the ledgers and checkpoints as the return surface, not the chat
Requires batched, one-line-decidable questions with a recommendation
Says the scheduler decides what it can and does not interrupt per item

evals.prompt: 我们四条线每轮巡检都在报同一类硬失败：同一棵树里几乎每一对单都被判 write_paths 重叠，落点全是 docs/implementation/status.md 和 tests/**。真要撞车的信号被这些噪声淹了。怎么办？
evals.expected_output: Names the root cause rather than the symptom: one executor runs one queue's orders strictly serially, so an overlap between two orders of that queue cannot produce two writers, and the validator cannot see that from the orders alone. Points at the queue-level declaration instead of per-pair serialize_with or per-order edits: a queue.json next to the orders with single_executor true plus the shared_paths the queue expects to share. States the edges: covered overlaps are exempted with one summary line, uncovered overlaps stay visible as NOTE lines that never fail the run, a malformed or incomplete declaration is a hard failure in every mode, no file means no behaviour change, and cross-queue overlap still fails (validate two queues together in one directory without queue.json). Does not propose a new role, does not change the order template, and does not weaken the cross-queue guard.
expectations: Explains that a single-executor queue cannot have two writers on one file, which is why the overlap is noise there
Prescribes one queue-level declaration (queue.json with single_executor and shared_paths), not per-pair serialize_with or per-order edits
Says uncovered overlaps stay visible as non-failing NOTE lines rather than being dropped silently
Says a declaration that cannot be read or is incomplete is a hard failure in every mode
Keeps the cross-queue guard: two queues validated together without queue.json must still fail
